judge: docs/testing/border_swatch_origin.py per captures<N>/ dir, plus docs/testing/fifo_skew_report.py on each logcat
prediction:
THE SELECTIVE (DRAW-ONLY) SKEW BOUND, accuracy side. Arm A is mainline with XEMU_OPT_FIFO_SKEW_BOUND = 0; arm B is the same tree with that one constant at 2 and nothing else -- the two refs differ by one hunk in one file. Texture border x10 on the nova, matching the disc_id and run count of the published noise floor (1789255594-exp54-stst-correct-3660183, disc_id = Texture border, 10 runs). Judge stale_px from docs/testing/border_swatch_origin.py, never differing pixels: the flake is combinatorial, each swatch has a fixed cost if it loses, and a run's total is the sum over whichever subset lost.

WHAT IS BEING TESTED, and it is NOT the mechanism -- the mechanism is settled. The every-submission bound (mode 1) already closed #44: stale_px 0 on 10 of 10 against 5 of 10 non-zero in its control, all three stale classes to zero, ab_compare PRE-REGISTERED PASS 20/20, held(n)/kicks = 1.0000 over 148,704 submissions. It also cost gfps p90 29 -> 13 and max 30 -> 15 on Galleon with the guest blocked 40.7% of wall clock. The question here is whether the SAME guarantee survives holding 826x less often. The guarantee is "no unprocessed DRAW sits in the FIFO while the guest runs", a submission carrying no draw adds no draw, and this disc makes 148,704 submissions for 180 draws.

V0 (GATE, arm A alone, and the pair is VOID without it): arm A's stale_px is non-zero on at least 3 of 10 runs. The published floor is 146, 0, 2352, 0, 0, 2430, 0, 1847, 5640, 181 -- five of ten. A control that does not flake cannot test a fix for a flake, and a zero from it would be an instrument result rather than a mechanism result.

V1 (THE BAR): arm B's stale_px == 0 on 10 of 10 runs, and all three stale classes -- torn, complete, partial-successor -- read zero. These classes fail for different reasons and cannot be added or subtracted, which is why each is named separately. FAILS on any non-zero run.

V2 (DID IT SELECT, which is this arm's whole subject): held(n) / kicks <= 0.05, against mode 1's 1.0000. This is the leg that separates "the selective bound works" from "the selective bound is the every-submission bound with extra code", and a stale_px of 0 cannot tell those apart because mode 1 also gives 0. Report scan(draw=) / scan(n=) alongside; on 180 draws in 148,704 submissions it should be well under 1%. FAILS above 0.05, and then the scan is not selecting and V1 passing proves nothing new.

V3 (THE PRE-SCAN MUST NOT BE THE COST): scan(ns=) summed over a window, divided by the window span, is under 2%. This is the trap the change is most likely to fall into, and it is invisible to every accuracy figure: the scan walks the same bytes, on the same thread, that the hold was waiting for, so moving the cost rather than removing it looks exactly like removing it. Mode 1's comparable number is the guest blocked 40.7% of wall clock. Report scan(words=)/scan(n=) as mean words per scan and scan(wmax=) as the worst. FAILS at 2% or more, and then selectivity has bought nothing and the repair is the scan, not the bound.

V4 (gave RE-MEASURED AGAINST THE NEW DENOMINATOR, and the prediction is that the hole MOVES rather than shrinks). Mode 1's S4 leg failed: gave = 1,002 of 148,704 submissions, 0.674%, against a registered bar of zero -- the pusher parking while stalled on a flip, a NOP acknowledgement or a context switch, none of which can clear until the guest runs again, so the alternative to releasing it is a deadlock. A selective bound changes WHICH submissions are covered, so the honest statement "impossible on the covered set, unlikely on the rest" needs the covered set named. PREDICTION: gave / held(n) >= 0.00674 -- the hole is at least as large a fraction of the covered submissions as it was of all of them, because the submissions that publish a draw are exactly the ones a flip is most likely to follow, so selectivity should CONCENTRATE the hole rather than dilute it. This leg FAILS if gave / held(n) < 0.00674, and that failure is the good outcome: it would mean the covered subset is cleaner than the whole and not merely smaller. Nothing in the patch forces either direction, which is what makes it a falsifier rather than a description of my own output. Report gave / kicks too, so the absolute fall is visible next to the rate.

V5 (THE FALLBACKS MUST NOT BE DOING THE WORK): (wrap + big) / held(n) < 0.20. The scan holds on three different findings and only one is the mechanism -- draw is a draw, wrap is a span that is not linearly addressable, big is the 16,384-word budget exhausted. If most holds are wrap or big then selectivity is nominal, and the failure mode that matters is that a hold rate rising under a heavy scene would read as the mechanism working when it is the budget running out. FAILS at 0.20 or more.

V6 (INTERNAL IDENTITIES, which must hold EXACTLY and not approximately): scan(draw=) + scan(nodraw=) + scan(wrap=) + scan(big=) == scan(n=), and held(n) == scan(draw=) + scan(wrap=) + scan(big=). Both are properties of the counters rather than of the host, so a violation is an instrument defect and voids every figure above it. An identity that holds exactly says the counters are read at one instant; one holding to +-1 says they are not, which is information about the instrument rather than noise.

V7 (must-not-move): ab_compare on the pair, same disc_id, same classifier_rev, 10 runs both arms -- nothing outside the measured run-to-run band, and the exact-capture count not below arm A's. Mode 1 gave 0 better / 0 worse / 17 same / 1 noise and exact 14 -> 15.

THE CAVEAT THAT TRAVELS WITH ANY VERDICT, unchanged from mode 1's: FIVE OF THE EIGHTEEN SWATCHES ARE STRUCTURALLY BLIND. The coloured checkerboard is position-indexed, so a larger image is a superset of a smaller one in-window and pass-1 1x1 through 16x16 render identically whether or not they lost their race. races_lost is a FLOOR. This change could take stale_px to 0 on 10 of 10 while still losing races on those five, and this instrument would call that a pass. What carries the rest is the impossibility argument plus V2 and V4, which read the bound directly.

AND THE NARROWING THAT IS NOT IN MODE 1: the 2D class reads guest memory outside a draw -- pgraph_image_blit and the surface-download paths. Mode 1 covers those; mode 2 does not. This is a deliberately narrower guarantee, scoped to the mechanism #44 measured texel-exact, and if a blit is ever shown to race, the method test is where it would be added. A V1 pass does not certify the blit path.
must_not_move: ab_compare: nothing outside the measured run-to-run band
exact-capture count not below arm A's
